claims: As of early April 2, 2026, the Artemis II crew is in a high-Earth orbit.
The Artemis II crew launched successfully from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026.
The Orion capsule is conducting systems tests.
The Orion capsule is preparing for a translunar injection burn to head toward the Moon.
The Artemis II crew is currently safe in orbit.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
The Orion capsule is nicknamed Integrity.
The Orion capsule is in an elliptical high-Earth orbit.
The Orion capsule has separated from the interim cryogenic propulsion stage (ICPS).
The Artemis II crew will remain in high-Earth orbit to test systems.
The Artemis II crew will execute a burn to travel toward the Moon.

Artemis II serves as a test for future lunar landings.
The Artemis II mission is expected to last roughly 9-10 days.
The Artemis II mission is expected to conclude with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
